Current Status of Ph.D. Research Work

1. Lower Bounds for Finite-Time Blow-Up in a Chemotaxis-Driven Tumor Growth Model:

The research article has been prepared. The current work involves reviewing the manuscript, improving the mathematical presentation, and reducing textual similarity while maintaining the originality and accuracy of the research.

2. Lower Bound Estimates for Finite-Time Blow-Up in a Multi-Species Keller–Segel Chemotaxis-Competition Model:

The manuscript was submitted for review but was rejected following the review process. The reviewer comments are being studied, and the manuscript is currently being revised to address the identified issues and reduce textual similarity before considering resubmission to a suitable journal.

3. Lower Bound Estimates for Finite-Time Blow-Up in a Fully Parabolic Two-Species Chemotaxis-Competition System with Singular Sensitivity:

The research is currently in progress. The main focus is on studying and verifying the mathematical derivations required to establish lower-bound estimates for the finite-time blow-up of solutions. The work involves energy estimates, rigorous inequality derivations, and an ODE comparison method to obtain a valid lower bound for the blow-up time.
